description.narrative: The Project is expected to increase access to finance for underserved MSMEs, including WMSMEs in Guinea. This is critical for Guinea in a context where the MSME finance gap is estimated at US$2.8 billion, or 19.1% percent of GDP, significantly constraining private sector development and inclusive growth. Guinea's financial sector remains shallow, with credit to the private sector representing only 9.1 percent of GDP, one of the lowest rates in West Africa. The majority of MSMEs operate informally and face significant barriers to accessing formal finance, including perceived high credit risk, lack of collateral, and the near-absence of affordable long-term funding. In this context, the Project will provide much-needed financing to assist underserved MSMEs including WMSMEs, in overcoming liquidity constraints and accessing capital to finance investments in inventory and inputs to sustain their economic activity. IFC also expects to encourage domestic banks to expand their MSME offerings, enhance competition, and potentially reduce borrowing costs. By demonstrating the viability of MSME lending in a challenging market, the Project can also inspire other financial institutions to scale up their MSME lending, further improving competition and access to finance across the sector.

The proposed investment consists of a 5-year senior loan of up to US$20 million to be disbursed in two equal tranches to Vista Gui (the Bank), the second largest bank in Guinea. The facility will contribute to increase access to longer-term financing for micro, small, and medium-sized enterprises (MSME) with at least 25 percent of loan proceeds dedicated to women-owned/led MSMEs (WMSMEs) in Guinea (the Project).
